thread:
kevin_support: FYI getting an escalation from a customer — consistent 250-600ms p95 for generate calls. They say traffic is landing in eu-west-1 but their org is pinned to us-east-1. Billing also shows eu tokens. Any routing/rollback running?

maria_sre: Seeing the alert too. ops-bot shows: `route-control fallback: triggered` for service=api, target_region=us-east-1 -> fallback_region=eu-west-1 at 2026-03-14T09:48:02Z. Investigating policy evaluation. :eyes:

ops-bot: ALERT: route-control.fallback.triggered {service: api, customer_id: acct-723, reason: capacity_shortage_us-east-1, fallback_region: eu-west-1, request_rate: 1200r/s} 

anna_ml: Can we confirm whether this was a forced fallback (policy) or a mis-eval (mapping mismatch)? I can pull routing-service logs.

sre-oncall: I'm on it. Pulling router logs now. Quick note: we had a short capacity blip in us-east-1 at 09:46 UTC due to a failed autoscale step. Autoscaler retried but failed to add the second GPU pool. Fallback was expected behavior but it shouldn't have applied to orgs pinned to a region — that's the abnormal part.

maria_sre: Found the regression. During the last rollout (2026-03-14 02:30 UTC) the route-policy merge logic changed order of precedence: previously org_pin > capacity_fallback, now it's reversed when policy has empty explicit_region list. This makes orgs with implicit pin (via org_metadata) eligible for fallback. Patch queued.

kevin_support: Customer is upset because latency spikes and they saw higher billing in eu-west. Can we manually force them back to us-east while we patch?

sre-oncall: Yes. Manual override pushed for acct-723: `POST /admin/routing/override` payload: `{ "customer_id": "acct-723", "region": "us-east-1", "expires_at": "2026-03-14T12:00:00Z", "reason": "incident manual override" }` — applied and confirmed by router echo header.

anna_ml: Repro steps we used to validate: 
1) `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Account-ID: acct-723" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` 
2) Check response header `x-redwood-region` -> was `eu-west-1` initially, now shows `us-east-1`.

kevin_support: Thanks. Customer confirmed traffic back in us-east and latency returned to normal. They're asking for root cause and ETA for permanent fix.

maria_sre: Root cause: policy precedence regression introduced in rollout 2026-03-14 02:30 UTC. Impact: ~12% of traffic for pinned orgs affected during capacity blip window (09:46-09:58 UTC). Billing impact: some token usage reported against eu-west for those orgs — finance will calculate charge reconciliation.

sam_prod: Do we have a short comms blurb for the customer? Keep it simple: what happened, what we did, next steps.

kevin_support: Draft for customer: "We experienced an automatic failover to eu-west-1 for a subset of pinned accounts due to a routing policy bug introduced in a recent rollout. We manually restored your pinned region, and we've deployed a patch to fix policy precedence. We're reviewing billing and will credit any cross-region usage caused by this incident." Thoughts?

maria_sre: Minor edits: include times (09:46-09:58 UTC) and mention the autoscaler failure as trigger. Otherwise LGTM.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: route-policy precedence fix deployed to prod at 10:22 UTC (deploy id: d-20260314-17). smoke tests passed.

anna_ml: Added e2e test to prevent regression: new test validates explicit org pin wins over fallback even when policy explicit_region is empty. Test PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4523

kevin_support: Filed billing ticket (#BILL-894) and customer notified with the blurb. Support will follow up with credits if finance approves.

maria_sre: Action items: 1) postmortem doc draft (assigned to me) 2) confirm billing reconciliation with finance (maria -> finance) 3) add observability alert to detect if pinned-org requests route outside pinned region (anna) 4) post-deploy monitor for 24h (sre-oncall).

sre-oncall: Will keep watch. I'll leave the manual override in place for 1h then remove if autoscaler stable.

kevin_support: Thanks team. I'll paste this thread into the customer ticket and link the postmortem when ready. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: NOTE: follow-up: autoscaler logs indicate root cause of failed scale: intermittent API error from cloud provider (rate-limit 429 on provisioning). We're opening provider support case.

maria_sre: I'll start the postmortem now and include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and OKRs for follow-up. Will ping when draft is ready for review.

kevin_support: Great. Closing thread here, please update postmortem and billing ticket with final numbers.

sre-oncall: last note — we've added a short-term mitigation: do not consider capacity_fallback for orgs with explicit org_policy.pin set until autoscaler SLA improved. We'll make it a configurable flag.
